question: Could local AI strengthen community without increasing surveillance?
drafted_with: Claude (Anthropic), directed and edited by Bentley
would_change: A deployed community system whose own users cannot say what it collects would restructure stations 4 and 5: the design station treats that as the failure to avoid, and a live counterexample would become the study object instead.

conditions.note: Filled in the walker, kept on your device, expires with the route.

stations.task: Read two pieces that assume different answers about where software and its data should live.

sources.title: Local-first software: you own your data, in spite of the cloud
sources.author: Martin Kleppmann, Adam Wiggins, Peter van Hardenberg, and Mark McGranaghan, Ink and Switch

sources.title: Privacy by Design: the seven foundational principles
sources.author: Ann Cavoukian, Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario

stations.task: Name one real coordination problem in a space you already move through: a library, a co-op, a block, a recurring gathering. Write down who it costs and what they do instead.
alternatives: If going out is not available today, use a space you know well from memory and say so in your notes.

stations.task: Speak with two people who hold different relationships to the problem: one who would use the thing you are imagining, and one who would carry its risks. Ask each what they would refuse.
State the strongest case that the thing you are sketching would centralize influence or expose people, using the source below rather than your own devil's advocate.

sources.title: Decentralization: an incomplete ambition, Journal of Cultural Economy
sources.author: Nathan Schneider

stations.task: Design one tiny service that works without accounts, tracking, or autonomous messaging. Two pages at most.
Ask one person to read the design and mark where the explanation fails. Record what changed in your own view and what stays open.

artifact.keeps: A two-page design: the need, the smallest useful function, what it knows, what it refuses to know, who is responsible for what, how it fails, and how a person leaves it.
